newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt says won't make RBA buy back gold.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt says won't make RBA buy back gold.

text.p: The Australian Government said on Monday it would be improper for it to order the Reserve bank of Australia (RBA) to repurchase gold reserves that the central bank had sold earlier this year.
"It would be improper for the government to order the Reserve Bank to buy back the gold," Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer told a mining conference here.
Parer said that the RBA was a "player in the market, just like anyone else," and that it needed to maximise its investments.

Earlier in July the RBA annouced that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold over the previous six months, reducing its holdings to 80 tonnes. The proceeds of the gold sales were reinvested in foreign government securities.
Australia's gold mining industry has complained to the government that the gold sales have undermined the nation's gold industry.
Australia is the world's third largest gold producing nation, with annual output nearing 300 tonnes.
Parer said the impact of the gold sales should be "kept in perspective," noting that the gold price had rebounded from their low point shortly after the sales were announced.
Gold prices hit a 12-year low of around US$314 an ounce after the sales were announced, but have now recovered to a current level of around US$325 an ounce.
Parer was delivering the speech in place of Prime Minister John Howard, who is in hospital with a serious case of pneumonia.
